prompt.title: Write your personal mission statement
prompt.text: Put into words what you want to be, what you want to do, and what you stand on. Start from what you've already written here: your values, your principles, your roles. It takes a few passes; the first one is enough for today.
prompt.glossText: The book calls this a personal mission statement: your own constitution, the thing you check decisions against.
prompt.whyItMatters: Without it, whoever shouts loudest sets your priorities. With it, a hard choice gets simpler: does this fit who I said I'd be? It also makes the rest of the habits point somewhere.
prompt.chapterReference: Habit 2: Begin with the End in Mind

step1.prompt: Which of the values you heard in your long views belong at the heart of this? Tap to keep them, or add your own.
step1.emptyText: No values yet. Do a long view first, or type what you already know matters.

step2.prompt: Which principles do you want your choices to rest on? Keep the ones you picked in Your centre, or add others.
step2.emptyText: No principles yet. Assess your centre first, or type the ones you want.

step3.prompt: For each role, one line: in this role, what do you want to be?
step3.roleLineLabel: In this role I want to be
step3.roleLinePlaceholder: e.g. the parent who asks a second question.
step3.emptyText: No roles yet. Name your roles first; they give the mission its shape.

step4.bePrompt: What kind of person do you want to be? Short lines, one quality each.
step4.doPrompt: What do you want to have done, or keep doing?
step4.maxHint: Ten is plenty. Combine two before adding more.

step5.prompt: Now write it as you'd say it. Use your values, principles and role lines; borrow from your collection. Rough is fine.
step5.draftPlaceholder: e.g. I want to be present with the people I love and honest in the work I do…

panel.title: Your collection
panel.usedText: Added to the end of your draft.
panel.emptyText: Your collection is empty. Add a few lines there and they'll show up here.
panel.noMatchText: Nothing in your collection matches these filters.

step6.prompt: Read it once out loud. Then answer honestly.
step6.emptyDraftHint: Write your draft first, then save a version.

review.roles: It covers every role that matters to me.
review.beAndDo: It says what I want to be and what I want to do.
review.principles: It rests on principles, not on moods or other people.
review.gladToLive: I'd be glad to live by it.

checklist.valueOrPrinciple: Choose or write one value or principle
checklist.roleLine: Write a line for one role

guide.inShort: You'll build a first mission statement in six short steps, starting from what you already wrote in Habit 2. Twenty to thirty minutes for a rough first version. You'll come back and improve it; that's the point.
howTo: Keep the values and principles that still ring true. Add any you're missing.
Write one line per role: in this role, what do you want to be?
List a few things you want to be, and a few you want to do.
Write the draft in your own voice. Borrow lines from your collection with "Use this".
Read it aloud and answer the five review questions. Fix what's missing.
Tap "Save version", then "Mark done". Revisit it in a month.

fields.label: Your mission statement
fields.value: I want to be present with the people I love and honest in the work I do. I keep my word, especially the small ones. At home I ask the second question. At work I give the credit away and build people who don't need me. I'd rather be trusted than impressive.

fields.label: Says what I want to be and do

guide.afterwards: Read it every Sunday when you plan your week. When a decision is hard, hold it against the statement. Rewrite a line whenever it stops sounding like you; each save becomes a version you can look back on.
